claims.text: The baseline is an as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu high-entropy-alloy coating on a conventional steel substrate without post-deposition heat treatment.
The controlled intervention is aging at approximately 600 °C for 1–4 hours under an inert atmosphere, followed by controlled cooling.
Aging the FeNiCrCoCu coating at approximately 600 °C will form well-dispersed nanoscale precipitates in the HEA matrix.
The nanoscale precipitates will impede dislocation motion during sliding.
The nanoscale precipitates will retard crack propagation during sliding.
Impeded dislocation motion and retarded crack propagation will reduce localized plastic deformation.
Impeded dislocation motion and retarded crack propagation will delay severe wear mechanisms.
The aged coating will have a significantly lower wear rate than the as-deposited coating during sliding at or above 500 °C.
The aged coating will exhibit a more homogeneous and less localized deformation pattern than the as-deposited coating during sliding at or above 500 °C.
The predicted effects are expected to hold during high-temperature sliding at or above 500 °C in an inert or controlled environment.
At or above 500 °C, thermal activation facilitates the dislocation mechanisms targeted by the nanoscale precipitates.
Excessive precipitate coarsening caused by deviations in aging parameters may eliminate the predicted benefit.
Over-aging may produce unwanted brittle phases.
Precipitation strengthening is well documented in high-temperature alloys.
